question.text: The SEBI (AIF) Regulations permit an AIF to be formed as any of the following EXCEPT:

answer.text: Trust under the Indian Trusts Act, 1882
Limited Liability Partnership under the LLP Act, 2008

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 8.4/8.5: permissible AIF forms are Trust, LLP, Company and Body Corporate (set up under an Act). Sole Proprietorship is NOT a permitted form — lacks a distinct legal identity from the individual. The Trap: Options A, B, C are all permitted. Option D is absurd but tempting for candidates unsure about body corporate. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B and C all test this permitted-forms question. Sample Question 1 of Chapter 8 in the workbook asks a similar question. Manager's Pro-Tip: If a sponsor insists on proprietorship for simplicity, refuse — the lack of entity separation exposes the proprietor's entire net worth to LP claims and fails the pooling principle.
